classification.difficultyReason: Combine two right-triangle tangent relationships using the difference between the horizontal distances.

content.prompt:
A scout measures the magnitudes of the angles of elevation to the top of a flagpole, $CD$, from two points ($A$ and $B$) at ground level. $A$ is 100 metres further away from the flagpole than $B$.

$A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ are in the one vertical plane. If the angles are $43^\circ$ and $14^\circ$, calculate the height of the flagpole, giving your answer correct to four significant figures.

spec.description: Horizontal points A, B, C in that order, vertical flagpole CD, sight lines AD and BD, elevation angles and the AB dimension. Ordinary source-blue geometry is black under house style.
spec.mathematics: AB = 100 m; angle DAC = 14 degrees; angle DBC = 43 degrees; CD perpendicular to AC.
spec.answerVisibility: All givens remain visible; no height or solution annotation is supplied.

answer.worked:
Let $BC=d$ metres and $CD=h$ metres. Then $AC=d+100$ metres.

$$\begin{align*}\tan43^\circ&=\frac{h}{d}\\d&=\frac{h}{\tan43^\circ}\\\tan14^\circ&=\frac{h}{d+100}\\d+100&=\frac{h}{\tan14^\circ}\end{align*}$$

Subtracting the two horizontal distances:

$$\begin{align*}100&=\frac{h}{\tan14^\circ}-\frac{h}{\tan43^\circ}\\h&=\frac{100}{\frac{1}{\tan14^\circ}-\frac{1}{\tan43^\circ}}\\h&\approx34.03\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

The flagpole is $34.03\text{ m}$ high, correct to four significant figures.
